title: Density transition for infinitely long cycles and Bose–Einstein condensation
literal_statement: For fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$ and dimension $d\ge 3$, determine whether the optimal point process(es) $P$ in $\chi^{(\le)}(\beta,\rho)$ have a loss of probability mass due to infinitely long cycles. The conjecture is that, for sufficiently small $\rho$, they do not have such a loss, whereas for sufficiently large $\rho$ they do; the latter phase is conjectured to be the Bose–Einstein-condensed phase.
technical_disposition: Requires the interacting-gas variational functional and all interaction assumptions; no full-density phase-transition mechanism. Paired record 396373 reverses the small/large density direction, so source reconciliation is essential.

title: BEC and loss of mass in infinite cycles for an interacting Bose gas
literal_statement: For fixed $\beta>0$ and dimension $d\ge 3$, determine whether the minimizer(s) $P$ in $\chi^{(\le)}(\beta,\rho)$ satisfy $\langle P,N^{(\ell)}_U\rangle<\rho$ for sufficiently small $\rho$, and do not satisfy this strict inequality for sufficiently large $\rho$ (equivalently, satisfy $\langle P,N^{(\ell)}_U\rangle=\rho$ there). The strict inequality is interpreted as a loss of probability mass corresponding to infinitely long cycles and is conjectured to characterize the Bose-Einstein-condensed phase.
technical_disposition: Literal small-density strict loss and large-density equality contradict the direction of paired 396372. Do not turn this transcription/scope conflict into a counterexample; functional and interaction hypotheses missing.

title: Counting rational matrices with a fixed irreducible characteristic polynomial
literal_statement:
Let $P(\lambda)=\lambda^n+a_{n-1}\lambda^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0$ be a monic polynomial with rational coefficients, irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, and, as assumed for simplicity in the report, split over $\mathbb{R}$. Let $V$ be the affine variety over $\mathbb{Q}$ of $n\times n$ matrices having characteristic polynomial $P(\lambda)$. For $v\in V(\mathbb{Q})$, write its coordinates over a common denominator and in lowest form, and define $\operatorname{Ht}(v)$ to be the maximum of the absolute values of the numerators and denominator. If $N_R=\#\{v\in V(\mathbb{Q}):\operatorname{Ht}(v)\le R\}$, then there exists a constant $C$ such that
\[
\lim_{R\to\infty}\frac{N_R}{R^{n(n-1)/2+1}}=C.
\]
technical_disposition: All irreducible totally real rational polynomials and growing rational height require arithmetic orbit counting. A diagonalization or n=2 calculation would not control denominators and the full asymptotic.

title: Precise value of the rectangle transformation cost
literal_statement: For rectangles with integer side lengths, define $E(a\times b,c\times d)$ as the minimum cost of transforming a rectangle of size $a\times b$ into one of size $c\times d$ using: (1) cutting a rectangle into two rectangles with integer side lengths; (2) gluing two rectangles along sides of equal length; and (3) deleting or creating a rectangle. Cutting or gluing along a side of length $l$ costs $l$ units, while deleting or creating a rectangle of size $a\times b$ costs $(a-1)(b-1)$ units. What is the precise value of $E(a\times b,c\times d)$?
technical_disposition: Primary Question 0.36 read with operations and neighboring cobordism bounds. Deletion/creation gives an upper bound, while cut/glue histories can use intermediate rectangles of unbounded dimensions. No matching lower-bound invariant or finite-state reduction established.
source_scope_note: Selected primary contribution; cited predecessor/successor bodies unread

title: Normality of semigroups associated with contingency tables
literal_statement: Let $r_1,\dots,r_N$ be natural numbers. An $r_1\times r_2\times\cdots\times r_N$ contingency table is a function $T:\{1,\dots,r_1\}\times\cdots\times\{1,\dots,r_N\}\to\mathbb Z_+$. Form the line-sum marginals and let $Ax=b$ denote the corresponding constraints on the table entries, collected in $x\in\mathbb Z_+^{r_1\cdots r_N}$, where $b$ is a vector of prescribed line sums. If $S_{r_1,\dots,r_N}$ is the semigroup generated by the column vectors of $A$, determine which of these semigroups are normal.
technical_disposition: Normality is lattice saturation for every dimension vector. Binary or two-dimensional integral cases do not classify general line-sum semigroups; no bounded universal hole certificate or classification route identified.

title: Banach frames for shearlet coorbit spaces
literal_statement:
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem 5: the irreducible unitary representation \(\pi\) is \(w\)-integrable; \(\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})\) is appropriately normalized and satisfies
\[
M\langle\psi,\pi(a,s,t)\psi\rangle:=\sup_{u\in(a,s,t)U}|\langle\psi,\pi(u)\psi\rangle|\in L^{1}_{w}(S);
\]
choose a neighborhood \(U\) of the identity \(e\) such that
\[
\|\operatorname{osc}_{U}\|_{L^{1}_{w}(S)}<\frac{1}{\|SH_{\psi}(\psi)\|_{L^{1}_{w}(S)}}.
\]
Then, for every \(U\)-dense and relatively separated family \(X=((a,s,t)_{\lambda})_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\subset S\), the family \(\{\pi((a,s,t)_{\lambda})\psi:\lambda\in\Lambda\}\) is a Banach frame for \(SC_{p,m}\):

1. \(f\in SC_{p,m}\) if and only if
\[
\big(\langle f,\pi((a,s,t)_{\lambda})\psi\rangle_{\widetilde H_{1,w}\times H_{1,w}}\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\in\ell_{p,m};
\]
2. \(\|f\|_{SC_{p,m}}\asymp\|\big(\langle f,\pi((a,s,t)_{\lambda})\psi\rangle_{\widetilde H_{1,w}\times H_{1,w}}\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\|_{\ell_{p,m}}\);
3. there is a bounded linear operator \(S:\ell_{p,m}\to SC_{p,m}\) such that \(S\big((\langle f,\pi((a,s,t)_{\lambda})\psi\rangle)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\big)=f\).
technical_disposition: Literal text is a Banach-frame conclusion under external Theorem 5, not a self-contained new conjecture. Missing coorbit/weight/oscillation definitions and parameter ranges; proving the displayed conclusion would risk reproducing the cited theorem.

title: Determining semi-effectivity of divisors on blow-ups of projective space
literal_statement:
Let \(\pi:X\to\mathbb{P}^N\) be the blow-up of a finite set of points \(p_1,\ldots,p_s\), let \(E_i=\pi^{-1}(p_i)\), and let \(H\) be the pullback of a hyperplane. Given
\[
D=dH-\sum_i m_iE_i,
\]
is there a procedure to determine whether \(D\) is semi-effective, i.e. whether \(h^0(X,kD)>0\) for some \(k>0\), or, alternatively, whether there are a \(t\) and a form \(F\) of degree \(td\) that vanishes at each point \(p_i\) to order at least \(tm_i\)?
technical_disposition: Positive semieffectivity can be semidecided by testing multiples, but failure of every multiple has no stopping certificate. Arbitrary point configurations and dimensions prevent a finite interpolation test from resolving the question.

title: Rationality of the Fano threshold
literal_statement:
Let $(X,E)$ satisfy the report’s Setup: $X$ is a complex projective Fano manifold of index $i_X$, $E$ is a rank-two vector bundle on $X$, $\rho(X)=1$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\simeq \mathbb{Z}H$ and $H$ ample, $H^4(X,\mathbb{Z})\simeq \mathbb{Z}H^2$, there is an unsplit covering family $M$ of rational curves on $X$, and $H\cdot \ell=1$ for $\ell\in M$. Normalize $E$ so that $c_1(E)=c_1H$ with $c_1\in\{0,-1\}$. For $\pi:\mathbb{P}(E)\to X$, define the Fano threshold by
$$t:=\inf\{u\in\mathbb{R}\mid -K_{\mathbb{P}(E)}+u\,\pi^*H\text{ is ample}\}.$$
Determine when $t\in\mathbb{Q}$.
technical_disposition: Rank-two bundle, Picard and curve hypotheses still leave nef/ample boundary rationality. Rational slopes on selected curves do not show a rational infimum; no full-scope cone description.

title: Determining the Mordell–Weil rank from a Weierstrass equation
literal_statement:
Let \cmathit{V}\omathrm\cto B be a non-trivial elliptic fibration with section, where \cmathit{V}\omathrm\and B are smooth projective varieties and \cmathrm\cdim B>1. Let \cmathcal L\omathrm\c be an ample line bundle on \cmathit{B}\omathrm\c, and let the associated Weierstrass fibration be
\[
W=\{y^2z=x^3+axz^2+bz^3\}\u0005subset \u0005mathbb P(\mathcal O\oplus\mathcal L^{-2k}\oplus\mathcal L^{-3k}),
\]
where \(k>0\) and \((a,b)\in H^0(B,\mathcal L^{4k})\times H^0(B,\mathcal L^{6k})\). Given \((a,b)\), determine the rank of \(\operatorname{MW}(\pi)\), the group of rational sections of \(\pi\), equivalently the group of \(K(B)\)-valued points of the generic fiber.
technical_disposition: Control characters and malformed macros obscure the literal fibration statement. General higher-dimensional base Mordell-Weil rank needs geometric/arithmetic input beyond a finite Weierstrass computation; no source repair or algorithm certificate.

title: Maximum number of zeros of Abelian integrals
literal_statement:
For fixed integers $m,n$, determine $Z(m,n)$, the maximum number of isolated zeros, counted with multiplicities, of the Abelian integrals
\[
I(h)=\oint_{\gamma_h}\bigl(f(x,y)\,dy-g(x,y)\,dx\bigr),
\]
where $H,f,g$ are real polynomials of degrees $m,n,n$, respectively, and $\{\gamma_h\}_{h\in(a,b)}$ is a family of ovals contained in the level curves $H=h$ and filling an annulus. The integral is assumed not to vanish identically on $(a,b)$, and the zeros are taken for $h\in(a,b)$.
technical_disposition: Uniform sharp zero count for every polynomial Hamiltonian and perturbation is a broad Abelian-integral problem. A fixed oval or low-degree calculation cannot determine Z(m,n).

title: The Lipschitz constant of the RSK correspondence
literal_statement:
Determine, for permutations $\pi,\tau\in S_n$ at adjacent-transposition distance $d(\pi,\tau)=t$, the maximum value of
\[
\Delta(\lambda(\pi),\lambda(\tau)):=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left|\lambda_i(\pi)-\lambda_i(\tau)\right|,
\]
where $\lambda(\pi)$ and $\lambda(\tau)$ are the Young-diagram shapes produced by the RSK correspondence, and $d$ is the least number of adjacent transpositions needed to transform $\pi$ into $\tau$.
technical_disposition: Adjacent transposition bounds from Greene invariants would need sharp joint realizability for every n,t. No extremal family with a matching upper bound was obtained; finite permutation tables would be instances only.

title: Maximum number of directed simplices in a d-tournament
literal_statement: For each integer $d\ge 2$, determine the greatest number of directed $(d+1)$-sets in a $d$-tournament on $n$ vertices. Here, an orientation of a $1$-set assigns it a sign; an orientation of a $2$-set is a direction on its edge; and, for $d\ge 3$, an orientation of a $d$-set consists of compatible orientations of all its $(d-1)$-subsets, meaning that any two induce different orientations on their common $(d-2)$-subset. A $d$-tournament is a set with an orientation on each of its $d$-sets, and a $(d+1)$-set is directed when its $d$-subsets are pairwise compatible. Equivalently, if $M_d(n)$ denotes this maximum, determine the constant $c_d=\lim_{n\to\infty}M_d(n)/\binom{n}{d+1}$, including its behavior for fixed small $d$ and as $d\to\infty$.
technical_disposition: Exact directed-simplex extremal numbers for all d,n are stronger than merely the limiting density. The record's equivalence wording cannot justify replacing the finite problem by an asymptotic bound; no short extremal mechanism.

title: Injectivity of Integral Invariants for Shape Identification
literal_statement:
Determine whether the two presented integral invariants—the circle-area invariant
\[
I_r^{\mathrm{Circle}}[\Omega](x):=\mathcal L^n(\Omega\cap B_r(x)),\qquad x\in\partial\Omega,
\]
for \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(r>0\), and the cone-area invariant
\[
I_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{Cone}}(\sigma):=\mathcal L^n(\Omega_\gamma\cap C_\varepsilon(\sigma)),\qquad \sigma\in S^{n-1},
\]
where
\[
\Omega_\gamma:=\{t\tau\in\mathbb R^n:0\le t<\gamma(\tau),\ \tau\in S^{n-1}\}
\]
for a non-negative continuous radial function \(\gamma\), and
\[
C_\varepsilon(\sigma):=\{t\tau:\tau\in S^{n-1},\ \langle\tau,\sigma\rangle\ge\cos(\varepsilon/2),\ t\ge0\},
\]
are injective mappings that uniquely identify the encoded object.
technical_disposition: Entire short Fidler report read, including both definitions, limitations and references. Cone transform is spherical-cap convolution of gamma^n; elementary null modes at selected apertures do not classify all apertures or resolve circle-area identification. The cited 2008 identifiability body and closest 2013 local-uniqueness body remain unread; no novelty clearance.
source_scope_note: Selected primary contribution; cited predecessor/successor bodies unread

title: Fixed point and law of large numbers for self-exciting correlated defaults
literal_statement:
Under all assumptions of Theorem 2, find an $\mathcal F^0$-adapted process $\alpha$ such that $\alpha=\Gamma(\alpha)$, where
\[
\Gamma_t(\alpha)=\int_0^t\mathbb E\!\left[\left.\varphi(s,B^0_{\cdot\wedge s},B^1_{\cdot\wedge s})\lambda(s,B^0_{\cdot\wedge s},B^1_{\cdot\wedge s},X^{0,\alpha}_s,X^{1,\alpha}_s,\alpha_s)e^{-Y^{1,\alpha}_s}\,\right|\,\mathcal F^0_s\right]ds.
\]
The report’s Theorem 3 asserts that such an $\alpha$ exists and, for this $\alpha$,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb E\left[\left|\bar L^n_t-\alpha_t\right|\right]=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb E\left[\left|\bar L^{n,\alpha}_t-\alpha_t\right|\right]=0.
\]
technical_disposition: Record explicitly attributes existence and LLN to Theorem 3 under all assumptions of external Theorem 2. Conditional fixed-point and coupling estimates require that setup; no independent open target isolated.

title: Equations defining the central curve of a linear program
literal_statement: For the linear program \(\max\{c^{T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), where \(A\) is a fixed rank-\(d\) matrix with \(n\) columns, determine polynomials defining the primal central curve without extraneous components. The report states that, if \(I_{A,b}\) is the linear ideal of \(\{Ax=b\}\) and \(J_{A,c}\) is the prime ideal of the central sheet \(L_{A,c}^{-1}\), then the prime ideal of the central curve is \(I_{A,b}+J_{A,c}\). Moreover, it is generated by the \(d\) linear polynomials given by \(Ax-b\) together with the circuit polynomials \(\sum_{i\in\operatorname{supp}(v)}v_i\prod_{j\in\operatorname{supp}(v)\setminus\{i\}}x_j\), where \(\sum_i v_i x_i\) ranges over the nonzero linear forms of minimal support vanishing on \(L_{A,c}\).
technical_disposition: Record itself gives prime ideal and circuit generators as a stated report result. Saturation/genericity and feasibility details would require the primary setup; re-proving these displayed generators supplies no eligible new outcome.

title: Equations of moment polyhedra of orbit projections
literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, let $K$ be a compact connected Lie subgroup, and let $\r\mathcal{O}\subset\mathfrak{g}^{*}$ be a coadjoint orbit. Assume that the orbit projection $\Phi_K:\mathcal{O}\to\mathfrak{k}^{*}$ is proper, and let $\Delta_K(\mathcal{O})$ be the intersection of $\Phi_K(\mathcal{O})$ with a fixed Weyl chamber of a maximal torus of $K$. Can one determine the equations defining the moment polyhedron $\Delta_K(\mathcal{O})$ in general?
technical_disposition: Every connected Lie group and proper coadjoint projection goes well beyond compact polytope examples. No finite general inequality-generating method established.

title: Spin-quantization commutes with reduction
literal_statement:
Let $(M,\omega,\Phi)$ be a compact Spin-prequantized Hamiltonian $K$-manifold, where $K$ is a compact connected Lie group. Let $\sigma$ be the smallest face of the closed Weyl chamber such that the Kirwan polytope $\Delta_K(M)$ is contained in the closure of $\sigma$. For a dominant weight $\mu\in\widehat K\cap\sigma$, set
\[
M^\sigma_\mu:=\Phi^{-1}(\mu+\rho-\rho_\sigma)/K_\sigma,
\]
where $\rho$ is the half sum of the positive roots, $\rho_\sigma$ is the half sum of the positive roots orthogonal to $\sigma$, and $K_\sigma$ is the common stabilizer of points in $\sigma$. With the reduced Spin-quantization defined by shift-desingularization when necessary, one has
\[
Q^{K}_{\mathrm{spin}}(M)=\sum_{\mu\in\widehat K\cap\sigma}Q_{\mathrm{spin}}(M^\sigma_\mu)V^K_\mu.
\]
technical_disposition: Literal equality is a Spin-quantization/reduction theorem with shift-desingularization dependencies. No novel question isolated; index-theoretic dependencies too large for a bounded short route.

title: Asymptotic behavior of analytic torsion in a degenerating Kähler family
literal_statement: Let $X$ be a connected Kähler manifold of dimension $n+1$, let $S\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the unit disc, and let $\pi:X\to S$ be a proper surjective holomorphic map with connected fibers such that $\pi(\Sigma_\pi)=\{0\}$, where $\Sigma_\pi$ is the critical locus of $\pi$. For $s\in S$, set $X_s=\pi^{-1}(s)$, equipped with the induced Kähler metric, and let $\xi$ be a holomorphic Hermitian vector bundle on $X$, with $\xi_s=\xi|_{X_s}$. Determine the behavior of the analytic torsion $\tau(X_s,\omega_{X_s}(\xi_s))$ as $s\to0$.
technical_disposition: General Kähler degeneration with Hermitian bundle requires singular-fiber and torsion asymptotics. No small local model resolves all degenerations or produces the requested complete behavior.

title: Norm-controlled inversion for polynomial off-diagonal decay matrices
literal_statement:
Let $B=B(\ell^2(\mathbb Z))$ and, for $s>1$, let $J_s$ be the Banach algebra of matrices $A=(A_{k,l})_{k,l\in\mathbb Z}$ with norm
$$
\|A\|_{J_s}=\sup_{k,l\in\mathbb Z}|A_{k,l}|(1+|k-l|)^s.
$$
Jaﬀard's and Baskakov's results show that $J_s$ is inverse-closed in $B$. Determine a norm-control function $h$ for this inclusion; that is, give an explicit function such that
$$
\|A^{-1}\|_{J_s}\le h\bigl(\|A\|_{J_s},\|A^{-1}\|_{B(\ell^2)}\bigr)
$$
whenever $A\in J_s$ is invertible in $B(\ell^2)$.
technical_disposition: Primary report Example 3 read. Later arXiv:1211.2974v1 section 3.3, Proposition 3.3(ii) and its proof give norm control for the identical J_r norm for every r>1. Parameter rename r=s and bounding operator norm by the summable decay envelope gives the requested two-norm function. Published-body reuse defeats discovery eligibility; Baskakov dependency not independently replayed and global registry still HOLD.
source_scope_note: Selected primary and successor proof section; dependencies not replayed

title: Nonlinear least-squares subspace approximation (Problem 1)
literal_statement: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, let $\mathcal{F}=\{f_1,\dots,f_m\}\subset H$ be a finite set, let $\mathcal{C}$ be a family of closed subspaces of $H$, and fix an integer $l\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal{V}=\{ \{V_1,\dots,V_l\}:V_i\in\mathcal{C},\ 1\le i\le l\}$. (1) Find the infimum of $e(\mathcal{F},\mathbf{V})=\sum_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\min_{1\le j\le l}d^2(f,V_j)$ over $\mathbf{V}=\{V_1,\dots,V_l\}\in\mathcal{V}$, where $d(x,V)=\inf_{v\in V}\|x-v\|_H$. (2) Determine whether there exists $\mathbf{V}_0\in\mathcal{V}$ such that $e(\mathcal{F},\mathbf{V}_0)=\inf\{e(\mathcal{F},\mathbf{V}):\mathbf{V}\in\mathcal{V}\}$, and find such a minimizing set if it exists.
technical_disposition: Finite assignment of data to l clusters reduces the objective to independent one-subspace infima, but attainment is not guaranteed for an arbitrary family C. This is a routine reduction rather than a new full solution; general minimizers need extra closure/compactness hypotheses. Related 2012 primary passage read, not the 2011 passage for this ID.
source_scope_note: Related 2012 passage only, not this ID primary

title: Limit process for online Quicksort
literal_statement:
For Quicksort run online on a list of $n$ distinct real numbers, let $X_n(l)$ be the number of comparisons made until the $l$-th smallest element appears, where $1\le l\le n$. With
\[
a_n(l)=\mathbb E[X_n(l)]=2n+2(n+1)H_n-2(n+3-l)H_{n+1-l}-6l+6,
\]
where $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number, define the normalized process on the grid $\{l/n:1\le l\le n\}$ by
\[
Y_n(l/n)=\frac{X_n(l)-a_n(l)}{n+1}.
\]
Does $Y_n$, viewed as a process in the index $l/n$, converge as $n\to\infty$ to a limiting process?
technical_disposition: Process convergence needs a specified interpolation and topology as well as joint recursive estimates, not just marginal expectations. No tightness or full limiting-process route identified.

title: Determination of wild-prime Euler factors for hypergeometric motives
literal_statement:
For hypergeometric data consisting of disjoint tuples \
a\ and \\b\ of equal cardinality, satisfying the stated cyclotomic-product condition, and for the associated motive \H(\a,\b;t)\ with \t\in\mathbf{P}^{1}(\mathbf{Q})\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\, determine in general the conductor \N\ and the precise Euler factors \P_p(T)\ at the wild bad primes \p\mid N\, namely those primes dividing the denominator of some parameter in \a\cup\b\.
technical_disposition: Parameter tuples and cyclotomic condition are external; wild local monodromy and conductor are not recovered from finitely many good-prime examples. Malformed macros retained; source-dependent scope HOLD.

title: Computing the admissible pair attached to a supercuspidal local component
literal_statement: Let $f$ be a modular newform of weight $k\ge 2$ and level $N$, and let $p$ be an odd prime such that the local component $\Pi_{f,p}$ is supercuspidal. Under the parametrization of supercuspidal representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ by admissible pairs $(E,\theta)$, where $E/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is quadratic and $\theta:E^\times\to\mathbb{C}^\times$ is a smooth character, compute the corresponding pair $(E,\theta)$, up to Galois conjugacy.
technical_disposition: Computing admissible character data for every odd-prime supercuspidal component requires local representation machinery and explicit input conventions. No bounded exact character reconstruction developed.

title: Conjecture on line transversals to homothetic disks
literal_statement:
Let \a0\(D\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be a disk. For a finite family of homothets \(\mathcal F=\{x_1+t_1D,\ldots,x_n+t_nD\}\), let \(T(k)\) mean that every subfamily with at most \(k\) members has a line transversal, and let \(\lambda_h(D,k)\) be the smallest \(\lambda_h>0\) such that \(T(k)\) for \(\mathcal F\) implies that \(\lambda_h\mathcal F\) has a line transversal. The conjecture is
\[
\lambda_h(D,3)=\sqrt{3}.
\]
technical_disposition: Homothetic disks allow varying scales. A three-center geometry calculation does not certify the transversal for every finite T(3) family; no sharp sqrt(3) construction and universal bound.

title: Eckhoff’s conjecture for line transversals to three translates of a disk
literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a disk in $\\mathbb{R}^2$. For a finite family $\\mathcal{F}$ of translates of $D$, let $T(3)$ mean that every subfamily of at most three members has a common line transversal, and let $\lambda(D,3)$ be the smallest $\lambda>0$ such that every such $T(3)$-family satisfies that $\lambda\mathcal{F}=\{x_i+\lambda D\}$ has a common line transversal. Eckhoff conjectured that

$$\lambda(D,3)=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}.$$
technical_disposition: Equal translates still require a global line fitting all centers under triplewise strip conditions. Regular-pentagon intuition is insufficient for a full golden-ratio extremal theorem; no primary/successor body clearance.

title: Coresets for the minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid
literal_statement:
For a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\operatorname{MEE}(S)$ denote the ellipsoid of minimum volume containing $S$, and let $\operatorname{DBM}$ denote the Banach–Mazur distance. For $\varepsilon>0$, define $f(d,\varepsilon)$ as the supremum, over all such $S$, of the minimum cardinality of a subset $X\subseteq S$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{DBM}\bigl(\operatorname{MEE}(X),\operatorname{MEE}(S)\bigr)\leq\varepsilon.
\]
Is $f(d,\varepsilon)=O(d/\varepsilon^2)$?
technical_disposition: Literal Banach-Mazur distance convention and epsilon normalization are missing; standard multiplicative distance is at least one. Unbounded or degenerate S may lack MEE. These wording/domain issues earn no discovery credit, and no full coreset theorem is certified.

title: General index problem in K-homology
literal_statement: Let $X$ be a finite CW complex. Given an element $\xi\in KK^0(C(X),\mathbb C)$, explicitly construct a K-cycle $(M,E,\varphi)$ on $X$ such that $\eta(M,E,\varphi)=\xi$. Here $M$ is a compact $\Spin^c$ manifold without boundary, $E$ is a complex vector bundle on $M$, $\varphi:M\to X$ is continuous, and $\eta(M,E,\varphi)=\varphi_*[D_E]$ is the analytic K-homology class determined by the Dirac operator on $M$ twisted by $E$.
technical_disposition: Surjectivity of geometric-to-analytic K-homology is a classical large dependency, while explicit construction from an arbitrary KK element needs input representation. No short full algorithm or small certificate.

title: Weighted Linear Matroid Parity
literal_statement: Let $A$ be a row-full-rank matrix with row set $U$ and column set $V$, where $r=|U|$ and $n=|V|$ are even. Partition $V$ into pairs, called lines, and let $w_\ell\in\mathbb{R}$ be the weight of each line $\ell$. The column dependence structure defines the matroid $M(A)$ on $V$. A base $B$ of $M(A)$ is a parity base if it is a union of lines. Find a minimum-weight parity base, where the weight of a parity base is the sum of the weights of its lines; denote the optimum by $\zeta(A,\Pi,w)$.
technical_disposition: Finite exhaustive parity-base enumeration solves the unqualified finite optimization wording, but is a routine algorithm and does not address the intended efficient weighted matroid-parity result. No credit for deleting a complexity requirement.

title: Maximum Non-\k\-Linked Induced Subgraph
literal_statement: A graph is said to be $k$-linked if it has at least $2k$ vertices and, for any ordered $k$-tuples $(s_1,\ldots,s_k)$ and $(t_1,\ldots,t_k)$ of $2k$ distinct vertices, it contains pairwise vertex-disjoint paths $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ such that $P_i$ connects $s_i$ and $t_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,k$. Given a graph $G=(V,E)$, find a vertex set $V_0\subseteq V$ of maximum cardinality such that the induced subgraph $G[V_0]$ is not $k$-linked.
technical_disposition: Enumerate induced subsets and all disjoint paths to solve the literal finite task. This is a routine finite-search restatement, not an eligible new maximum-subgraph theorem or efficient algorithm.

title: Convergence analysis for the surface Taylor–Hood discretization
literal_statement: Determine whether the planar convergence analysis for the quadratic–linear Taylor–Hood element (\P_2\–\P_1\) extends to the corresponding discretization on immersed hypersurfaces for the locally area-preserving \H^1\ Willmore flow. If it does, establish the expected order-two convergence for the velocity \v\ in the \V\ norm and the tension field \\sigma\ in the \H\ norm, while accounting for the geometric-approximation error of the hypersurface.
technical_disposition: Surface geometry error and discrete inf-sup stability must be controlled along a time-dependent Willmore flow. A planar Taylor-Hood proof analogy alone is no subsumption bridge or surface convergence proof.

title: Extrapolation of a stationary stochastic process from a finite time interval
literal_statement:
Let $X=(X_t)_{t\\in\mathbb R}$ be a second-order weakly continuous, weakly stationary stochastic process on $(\Omega,\mathcal A,P)$ with $EX_t=0$. For $a>0$, suppose $X$ is observed for $-a\le t\le a$, and let
$$
H(X):=\operatorname{c.l.s.}\{X_t:t\in\mathbb R\}\subset L^2(\Omega,\mathcal A,P),
$$
$$
H(X;a):=\operatorname{c.l.s.}\{X_t:t\in[-a,a]\}\subset H(X),
$$
with $H(X)\ne H(X;a)$. Determine the best mean-square prediction of $X_s$ for $s\notin[-a,a]$, equivalently, determine the orthogonal projection of $X_s\in H(X)$ onto $H(X;a)$.
technical_disposition: Orthogonal projection exists by Hilbert-space theory; explicit prediction requires spectral measure and closed span information. Merely restating a normal equation supplies no new full-scope predictor.

title: Explicit density of the invariant measure for the even continued-fraction set
literal_statement: Let $E_{\rm even}$ be the set of all irrational numbers in $[0,1]$ whose continued-fraction expansion entries are all even, and let $h$ be its Hausdorff dimension. It was known that the $h$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $E_{\rm even}$ vanishes, while its $h$-dimensional packing measure $P_h$ is positive and finite. The Gauss map $G$ restricted to $E_{\rm even}$ admits a unique probability $G$-invariant measure $\bc$ equivalent to $P_h$, and the Radon–Nikodym derivative $d\bc/dP_h$ has a unique real-analytic extension to the whole interval $[0,1]$. The problem is to find a closed explicit formula for this derivative, or else to show that no such formula exists.
technical_disposition: Real-analytic density existence does not define what counts as a closed formula or its impossibility. A transfer-operator fixed point is only an implicit characterization; no explicit density or impossibility theorem.

title: Bayesian estimation of the Hurst parameter from discrete fractional Brownian-motion increments
literal_statement:
For a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$, observe a single realization $X^{\widehat H}$ with true parameter $\widehat H$ at the equidistant times $t_j=j/n$, $j=0,1,\ldots,n$. Define the increments
\[
Y^{\widehat H}_j:=X^{\widehat H}(t_j)-X^{\widehat H}(t_{j-1}),\qquad j=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Assuming the noninformative prior stated in the report, determine the conditional probability distribution of $H$ given $(Y^{\widehat H}_1,\ldots,Y^{\widehat H}_n)$, and construct estimators of the true parameter $\widehat H$ from this conditional distribution.
technical_disposition: Gaussian increment covariance yields likelihood determinant/inverse and Bayes normalization once the prior is specified. The record leaves the noninformative prior external; this routine likelihood calculation alone is not a novel estimator theorem.

title: Nonlinear regularization for the two-dimensional Calderón inverse conductivity problem
literal_statement: Construct a family of continuous mappings $R_\alpha:Y\to X$, $0<\alpha<\infty$, for the forward map $F(\sigma)=\Lambda_\sigma$ such that, for each fixed $\sigma\in D(F)$, $$\lim_{\alpha\to0}\|R_\alpha(\Lambda_\sigma)-\sigma\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}=0,$$ and choose a regularization parameter $\alpha=\alpha(\delta)$ with $\alpha(\delta)\to0$ as $\delta\to0$ so that the worst-case reconstruction error $$\sup_{\Lambda^\delta_\sigma\in Y}\left\{\|R_{\alpha(\delta)}(\Lambda^\delta_\sigma)-\sigma\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}:\|\Lambda^\delta_\sigma-\Lambda_\sigma\|_Y\le\delta\right\}$$ tends to zero as $\delta\to0$.
technical_disposition: Continuity of each regularizer plus pointwise L-infinity reconstruction requires the exact conductivity domain and data norms. General inverse-problem heuristics and a priori compact subclasses do not resolve full stated scope.

title: The missing interfacial flow rule in heterogeneous small-strain elastoplasticity
literal_statement:
In a perfect small-strain elastoplastic evolution without inertia or body loads, driven by a boundary displacement, consider an interface between phases $i$ and $j$, with associated sets of admissible stresses $K_i$ and $K_j$. Writing $
u$ for the interface normal and $(\cdot)_\tau$ for the tangential part, the proposed missing interface flow rule is

$$
\dot u_i-\dot u_j\in N_{(K_i\nu)_\tau\cap(K_j\nu)_\tau}\bigl((\sigma^D\nu)_\tau\bigr),
$$

where $N_C(\xi)$ denotes the normal cone to $C$ at $\xi$. The report presents this rule as necessary to determine the possible plastic slip along the interface and to ensure Hill’s maximum plastic work principle.
technical_disposition: The proposed interface normal-cone rule is already stated, with evolution/trace and admissible stress assumptions external. No well-posedness or necessity/sufficiency proof follows from the displayed formula alone.

title: Integral representations for intermediate coefficients in zeta-value linear forms
literal_statement:
For the coefficients $a_2,\ldots,a_{n-1}$ occurring in the linear form
$$
\int_0^1\!\cdots\!\int_0^1 \frac{x_1^{h_1}(1-x_1)^{j_1}\cdots x_n^{h_n}(1-x_n)^{j_n}}{\bigl(1-(1-x_1\cdots x_{n-1})x_n\bigr)^{j_n+h_1-k+1}}\,dx_1\cdots dx_n
= a_1+a_2\zeta(2)+\cdots+a_{n-1}\zeta(n-1)+a_n(n-1)\zeta(n),
$$
under the hypotheses $n\ge 2$, $h_1,\ldots,h_n,j_1,\ldots,j_n,k\ge 0$, and $h_r+k-h_1\ge 0$ for $r=2,\ldots,n-1$, find integral representations analogous to the stated contour-integral representation for $a_n$.
technical_disposition: All intermediate coefficients for every admissible exponent tuple require the primary decomposition and contour definitions. Low n identities or formal differentiation do not give a full integral family.

title: Bubbling-off solutions and threshold behavior for the critical focusing nonlinear wave equation
literal_statement:
For radial solutions of the energy-critical focusing nonlinear wave equation \(\Box u=-u_{tt}+\Delta u=-u^5\) on \(\mathbb{R}^{3+1}\) with energy close to, but slightly larger than, that of the radial ground state \(W\), construct bubbling-off solutions of the form
\[
u(t,x)=W_{\lambda(t)}(x)+\varepsilon(t,x),
\qquad W_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{1/2}W(\lambda x),
\]
where \(\lambda(t)\) follows various possible dynamics, and determine the significance of these solutions as threshold behavior separating stable blow-up and scattering regimes for data near the ground state.
technical_disposition: Construction with various scale dynamics and classification of near-threshold radial wave behavior require a substantial nonlinear PDE argument. A single ansatz or prescribed scale is only a parameter instance.

title: Optimal union of subspaces for subspace segmentation
literal_statement:
Let $B$ be a Banach space and let $W=\{w_1,\ldots,w_N\}\subset B$ be a finite set. For $i=1,\ldots,M$, let $\mathcal C_i$ be a family of closed subspaces of $B$, each containing $\{0\}$, and let $\mathcal C=\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_M$. Given $0<p\leq\infty$ and an integer $M\geq1$:

(i) Find the infimum of
\[
e(W,V):=\sum_{w\in W}\min_{1\leq j\leq M} d^p(w,S_j),
\]
over $V=\{S_1,\ldots,S_M\}\in\mathcal C$, where $d(x,y):=\|x-y\|_B$.

(ii) Find a sequence of $M$-subspaces $V^o=\{S_1^o,\ldots,S_M^o\}\in\mathcal C$, if it exists, such that
\[
e(W,V^o)=\inf\{e(W,V):V\in\mathcal C\}.
\]
technical_disposition: Primary Problem 1 and following paragraphs read. Report explicitly cites known p=2 Hilbert-space necessary/sufficient conditions, while general p remains open there. Partition enumeration reduces to arbitrary single-subspace minimization, so it does not supply attainment for arbitrary C_i; p=infinity convention also needs clarification. No routine reformulation credited.
source_scope_note: Selected primary contribution; cited predecessor/successor bodies unread

title: Efficient inversion of phaseless frame measurements
literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space and let $\mathcal{F}=\{f_1,\ldots,f_m\}$ be a frame for $H$. With the equivalence relation $x\sim y$ if $y=zx$ for a scalar $z$ satisfying $|z|=1$, define $\widehat H=H/\sim$ and
$$
\varphi:\widehat H\longrightarrow(\mathbb{R}^{+})^m,
\qquad \varphi(\widehat{x})=\bigl(|\langle x,f_k\rangle|^2\bigr)_{1\le k\le m}.
$$
The problem is to determine when $\varphi$ is injective and, when it is injective, to find fast or efficient algorithms for inverting it.
technical_disposition: Injectivity alone and efficient inversion in both real and complex dimensions are separate demands. Complement property handles a real criterion, not the complex case and efficient inversion; no full combined route.

title: Density estimation from an unweighted random $k$-nearest-neighbor graph
literal_statement: Assume we draw points $X_1,\dots,X_n$ independently and identically distributed from some nice density $p$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Construct the unweighted, undirected $k$-nearest-neighbor graph by connecting $X_i$ to $X_j$ whenever $X_i$ is among the $k$ nearest neighbors of $X_j$, and let $A$ be its adjacency matrix. Can we estimate the density $p(X_i)$ at the data points, up to constant factors, using only the adjacency matrix $A$?
technical_disposition: Adjacency is unchanged by similarities of the sampled point cloud, while density rescales. The allowed up-to-constant interpretation could absorb this; no wording-based nonidentifiability promoted. General nice-density assumptions and statistical accuracy regime missing.

title: Hexagonal conjecture for spectral minimal partitions
literal_statement:
Let \d4aa be the planar domain under consideration, let \d49c(\d4aa) denote its area, and let \d40b_k(\d4aa) be the infimum, over all partitions of \d4aa into \d458 open sets, of the maximum of their ground-state Dirichlet eigenvalues. If \(\operatorname{Hexa}_1\) denotes the regular hexagon of area \(1\), prove the hexagonal conjecture
\[
\lim_{k\to+\infty}\frac{L_k(\Omega)}{k}=\lambda(\operatorname{Hexa}_1)\,A(\Omega)^{-1}.
\]
technical_disposition: Malformed domain macros retained. Sharp asymptotic hexagonal spectral partition energy requires universal lower bound and boundary control; tiling upper bounds alone are insufficient.

title: Ground-state energy minima for a random displacement in an equilateral triangle
literal_statement:
Let $D$ be an equilateral triangle, and let $q$ be a smooth, compactly supported potential whose support has no holes and which has the same reflection symmetries as $D$ (for example, $q$ may be radially symmetric). For translations $a$ such that $\operatorname{supp} q(\cdot-a)\subset D$, define
\[
G=\{a\in\mathbb R^2:\operatorname{supp} q(\cdot-a)\subset D\}.
\]
Let $E_0(a)$ be the smallest eigenvalue of
\[
H=-\Delta+q(\cdot-a)
\]
on $D$ with Neumann boundary conditions. Prove that $E_0$ is either identically zero on $G$ or has strict minima at the corners of $G$.
technical_disposition: All smooth hole-free symmetric potentials include both signs. Triangle reflection heuristics do not imply strict corner minima; no exact spectral counterexample or maximum principle route established.

title: Discrete uniformization of triangulated surfaces
literal_statement: Given a discrete metric on a triangulated surface, find a discretely conformally equivalent Euclidean, spherical, or hyperbolic metric without cone-like singularities at the vertices, meaning that the sum of the angles of the corresponding triangles around every vertex is $2\pi$. The report states that for triangulated surfaces of genus $g=0$, $g=1$, or $g>1$, the resulting metric is respectively spherical, Euclidean, or hyperbolic.
technical_disposition: Definition of discrete conformal equivalence and admissible triangulation moves missing. Gauss-Bonnet gives only curvature compatibility, not construction; reproducing known uniformization framework would not be new.

title: Minimal-area branched surface associated with a knot or link isotopy type
literal_statement:
For a given non-trivial isotopy type of knots (or links), find, approximately and numerically, a 2-dimensional branched surface \(M\) (a standard spine, possibly with 1-dimensional parts) of minimal area such that there exists a knot (or link) \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}\) of the given isotopy type satisfying
\[
 d(M,K)=1,
\]
and such that \(M\) is a deformation retract of \(\mathbb{R}^{3}\setminus K\).
technical_disposition: Numerical minimum for every knot/link needs admissible branched-spine class, area compactness and precise distance convention. A mesh heuristic is not a certified global minimum; no small full-scope route.

title: Openness of minimizers in spectral shape optimization
literal_statement: Let $k,N\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $F:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and non-decreasing in each variable. For quasi-open sets $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ of unit volume, minimize $F(\lambda_1(\Omega),\ldots,\lambda_k(\Omega))$, where $\lambda_i(\Omega)$ are the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the standard Laplacian. Determine whether the minimizers in this general setting are necessarily open.
technical_disposition: For constant F every unit-volume quasi-open representative is a minimizer, so literal openness needs representative conventions. Null-set modifications and such degeneracy are wording corrections, not substantive spectral-shape discoveries; no credit sought.

title: Traverso’s isomorphism-number conjecture for p-divisible groups
literal_statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $D$ be a $p$-divisible group over $k$ of positive height $r$. Write $(M,\varphi,\vartheta)$ for its contravariant Dieudonné module, set $d=\dim_k(M/\varphi(M))$, $c=\dim_k(M/\vartheta(M))$, and $t=\min\{c,d\}$. Let $n_D$ be the smallest $n\in\mathbb N^*$ such that the isomorphism class of $D$ is uniquely determined by $D[p^n]$. Traverso’s conjecture asserts that, if $cd>0$, then $n_D\le t$.
technical_disposition: General p-divisible groups require isomorphism-number bounds beyond a finite Dieudonné module sample. Suspected established results/refutations need actual bodies; no primary or successor proof read, so no resolution claim.

title: Asymptotic Minimum Dilatation Problem
literal_statement: Let \(\mathcal P=\bigcup_S\mathcal P(S)\) be the set of pairs \((S,\varphi)\), where \(S=S_{g,n}\) is an oriented surface of finite type and \(\varphi\) is a pseudo-Anosov mapping class on \(S\). For \((S,\varphi)\in\mathcal P\), define the normalized dilatation by \(L(S,\varphi)=\lambda(\varphi)^{|\chi(S)|}\). The smallest known accumulation point of the image of \(L\) is \(\ell_0=\left(\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\right)^2\). Is there an accumulation point for the image of \(L\) that is smaller than \(\ell_0\)?
technical_disposition: Needs a genuine accumulation sequence below the given normalized dilatation, not one pseudo-Anosov example. No small family with a certified limiting polynomial root and surface complexity established.

title: Correct hypotheses for comparing invariant algebra deformations with abstract scheme deformations
literal_statement: Let $X=X'/G$ be a scheme presented as a good quotient of a quasi-affine scheme $X'$ by a linearly reductive group $G$, with $X'$ an open invariant subscheme of an affine $G$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}S$. Determine the correct hypotheses under which the comparison morphism of deformation functors $\operatorname{Def}^{G}S\to\operatorname{Def}_{X}$ is an isomorphism for abstract deformations of $X$, taking account of infinitesimal automorphisms and the loci where the quotient has non-finite isotropy.
technical_disposition: Correct comparison hypotheses for quotient deformation functors require cotangent/local-cohomology and isotropy analysis. One smooth/free quotient case or extra strong sufficient assumptions cannot classify the full question.

title: Problem 8: Cohomology of open wonderful models of hyperplane arrangements
literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an arrangement of hyperplanes in $\mathbb P^\ell$. Let $\pi:X\to\mathbb P^\ell$ be the De Concini–Procesi wonderful model of $\mathcal A$ corresponding to the minimal building set $\mathcal G$. For $Y\in\mathcal G$, let $D_Y\subseteq X$ be the corresponding boundary divisor. Let $\mathcal G_1\subseteq\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal G_1$, and let
\[
U=X\setminus\bigcup_{Y\in\mathcal G_1}D_Y.
\]
Use toric methods to compute $H^*(U,\mathbb C)$, and determine the pairs $(\mathcal A,\mathcal G_1)$ for which $H^p(U,\mathbb C)=0$ for $p>\ell$.
technical_disposition: Arbitrary arrangement/building-set open models require full cohomology and vanishing classification. Standard complement or full compactification cases do not answer intermediate boundary deletions.

title: Definable $(k,k)$-theorem for NIP theories
literal_statement:
Assume $T$ has NIP. Let $\theta(y)$ and $\formulax$ be formulas, and let $d\in\boldsymbol{N}$ satisfy $d>\vc^*(\formulax)$. Suppose that the family $\{\formulax(x;a):\models\theta(a)\}$ is $d$-consistent. Can one find formulas $\theta_i(y)$, $i=1,\ldots,t$, such that
\[
\theta(y)\to\bigvee_{i=1}^{t}\theta_i(y),
\]
and, for each $i$, the family $\{\formulax(x;a):\models\theta_i(a)\}$ is consistent?
technical_disposition: NIP, dual VC dimension and d-consistency must imply a finite definable refinement with global consistency. Finite combinatorial (p,q) covering alone does not produce definable cells; no bounded logical construction or proof route.
